weeks.title: Sound Design: Music Selection, Mood and Audio Balance

quiz.title: Module 3 — Tuesday — Sound Effects and Audio Layering
quiz.description: Tuesday's quiz covers the purpose of sound design, why vocals carry the story, ambience against Foley, J-cuts and L-cuts, reverb for space, EQ, what a high-pass filter removes, and why mixing and normalisation matter before publishing.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of sound design in filmmaking?
options: To make videos longer
To create an immersive experience and connect viewers to what is happening on screen
To replace visual storytelling
To reduce the number of video clips
questions.explanation: Sound is what puts the viewer inside the scene. It carries atmosphere and emotion that the picture alone cannot, which is why a weak mix makes good footage feel flat.

questions.prompt: Which audio element is usually the most important in a video because it carries the story and information?
options: Background music
Ambience
Vocals, including dialogue and voice-over
Creative sound effects
questions.explanation: Everything else supports the voice. If dialogue or narration is buried, the viewer loses the story no matter how good the music is.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between ambience and Foley?
options: Ambience establishes the background environment, while Foley involves recording sounds that match on-screen actions.
Ambience is used for dialogue, while Foley is used for music.
Ambience creates transitions, while Foley changes video colours.
Ambience removes background noise, while Foley increases volume.
questions.explanation: Ambience is the bed a location sits on — traffic, room tone, weather. Foley is performed to picture, rebuilding the specific sounds of the actions on screen.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between a J-cut and an L-cut?
options: A J-cut removes audio, while an L-cut removes video.
A J-cut introduces the next scene's audio before the visual cut, while an L-cut allows the previous scene's audio to continue after the visual cut.
A J-cut increases volume, while an L-cut decreases volume.
A J-cut adds music, while an L-cut adds sound effects.
questions.explanation: The names describe the shape on the timeline. In a J-cut the incoming audio leads its picture; in an L-cut the outgoing audio trails behind it.

questions.prompt: What is the primary purpose of using reverb in audio editing?
options: To remove dialogue from a video
To increase the speed of audio
To create a sense of space and make sounds fit their environment
To remove all high frequencies
questions.explanation: Reverb adds the reflections of a physical space. A dry sound in a large room feels wrong; the reverb tells the ear how big the space is.

questions.prompt: What is EQ (Equalization) used for in audio editing?
options: To adjust or control different audio frequencies
To add transitions between video clips
To increase video resolution
To synchronize subtitles with dialogue
questions.explanation: EQ shapes the frequency balance — cutting mud, lifting presence, taming harshness. It changes the tone of a sound, not its timing or volume.

questions.prompt: What happens when a high-pass filter is applied to audio?
options: It removes high frequencies.
It increases all frequencies.
It removes low frequencies.
It removes the entire audio track.
questions.explanation: A high-pass filter lets the high frequencies pass and rolls off the low ones. It is the standard fix for rumble, wind and handling noise.

questions.prompt: Why is audio mixing and normalization important before publishing a video?
options: To make every sound equally loud
To ensure audio levels are balanced and prevent unwanted clipping or peaking
To remove all background music
To increase the video's frame rate
questions.explanation: Mixing balances the elements against each other; normalisation keeps the overall level in range. Clipping cannot be undone once it is exported.
